notes:
Added
- Character names are spelled right far more often. Kirinuki now knows how the Dragon Ball Super dub spells its characters, techniques and places (Beerus, Whis, Kamehameha, Tournament of Power and about 160 more), tells the speech recogniser which names to listen for, and fixes names it still hears wrong, such as "Bira" for Beerus. Everyday words like "hit", "cell" or "pan" are left alone.
- Names and terms (Settings → Captions, and Style Studio → Name spellings): add a name and how it is often misheard, choose which names are listened for, and accept or dismiss suggested names for a newly identified series. A meter shows how many names the recogniser listens for. When you correct the same word the same way three times, Kirinuki offers to remember it.
- Every clip's captions are checked before you approve it. A clip where people speak but no captions were made says "Captions missing: fix before approving" and can't be approved or uploaded until you choose what to do: transcribe it again, keep it as it is, or not use it. Clips where nobody speaks, and songs, say so instead of failing quietly.
- Picked clips are listened to a second time, with the music removed when the music-removal model is downloaded, so shouted lines under loud music get their captions. Moments where nobody speaks are no longer picked as clips.
- Caption words appear when they are said: an optional word-timing model (about 360 MB, downloaded from Kirinuki's own release page) lines every word up with the speech.
- Optional "Best accuracy" captions on PCs with an NVIDIA graphics card: a larger speech model (about 3.1 GB), offered after your first job and downloaded only if you choose it.
- AI proofreading, on by default when your Claude or ChatGPT account is connected (it uses the allowance-saving model): it can only swap a misheard word for one of the names in your list, every change is shown with Accept and Revert, and you can turn it off in Settings → Captions.
- A simpler Style Studio. One large preview with a panel beside it: Quick edit holds the things people change most, and Captions, Watermark, Hook, Layout and Publishing each have their own panel. "Advanced" shows every other setting in place, and "Search settings" jumps straight to any of them. Choices are pictures and colour chips instead of long forms, and fonts are listed in their own lettering.
- The watermark maker walks you through a mark in a few short steps, and the brand kit is one calm page. "New style from my brand kit" makes a style from your kit's fonts, colours and mark, and your brand colours and fonts come first in every picker.
- Choose how each clip fills the vertical frame: Fit (the whole picture), Fill (zoomed in) or Cinematic (the whole picture between black bars). With Fill, drag the crop box on the preview, or use the arrow keys, to choose what stays in view and how far it zooms. It is always your choice: nothing moves or zooms by itself.

Fixed
- The preview no longer makes each frame twice after a change, so the frames beside it stop reloading a moment later and the status line shows how long the new frame really took; screen readers can also read that status line in the Style Studio.
- Turning the watermark on no longer shows nothing when the brand kit is empty, and the preview now jumps to a moment where the mark shows instead of the hook card.
- A clip's captions can no longer come out empty without a warning: when a clip had words but none were drawn, its check fails and says so.
- A job folder that Windows kept busy for a moment is now removed on a later try instead of staying behind.
- Keyboard users reach the preview's row of frames and the brand kit's "On this page" list with one Tab and move inside them with the arrow keys, and "Reduce motion" now stops every transition.
- A clip that sounds like a song now waits for you to choose "Approve without captions" instead of going out without captions on its own, and dialogue shouted over an insert song keeps its captions.
